text.p: Italian bond futures slipped back in early trade following on Wednesday's decline due to lower U.S. T-bonds and German bunds, and the absence of an Italian interest rate cut after a further fall in Italian inflation.

Preliminary data from 11 Italian cities on Tuesday and Wednesday pointed towards a CPI May rate of 1.5/1/6 percent after April's 1.7 percent and many dealers had been expecting a discount rate cut late Wednesday.
Many dealers expected a rate cut of 50 to 75 basis points in the discount rate in the coming weeks, but there was dismay the Bank of Italy has been so cautious on cutting rates.
Dealers said that many operators were on hold ahead of the likely release of the government's three year DPEF economic plan next week and the Bank of Italy's annual assembly.
"The market is awaiting a rate cut, but it is a long time coming," said one LIFFE trader.
